question: Five short studies run as one batch (see each entry).

E01.question: Which low-cost model handles everyday assistant and ops tasks best?
E01.setup: 10 assistant/ops tasks, one-shot, no tools, one run per model; graded blind by gemini-3.7-flash (not a candidate). Candidates were limited to models available through the router at the time.
E01.finding: deepseek-v4.1-flash passed 10/10; glm-5.3-flash and deepseek-v4-flash each missed T2 (a fair-code license nuance).

rerun.run: E01 re-run of T1-T7 with the same grader
rerun.finding: The ranking held over two runs: deepseek-v4.1-flash >= glm-5.3-flash > deepseek-v4-flash. T4 (triage of a scheduled job that exited with code 3) failed for every model in the re-run, which points to task ambiguity or grader strictness rather than model capability. T2 is the only consistent differentiator (deepseek-v4-flash missed it both times).

limitations: one run per cell in the first pass

E02.experiment: E02: is a premium advisor model worth it?
E02.question: Do pricier models do clearly better on harder advisory tasks?
E02.setup: 5 advisory tasks, one-shot. Candidates: deepseek-v4-pro and gemini-3.7-flash (kimi-k2.6 is covered by E08b). Graded twice: by gpt-6-luna, then by gemini-3.7-flash.

grader1_gpt-6-luna.note: the grader's output was ambiguous about which answer belonged to which model

E02.finding: The two graders disagreed completely: gemini-3.7-flash passed all 10 answers (including its own), gpt-6-luna passed 2 of 5 for each model. The original write-up said luna failed all 10, which does not match its recorded scores; because luna's output was ambiguous about which answer was which, neither figure is reliable. The question stays open; E08b is the closest evidence.

E03.question: Which model compresses a long text without losing or inventing facts?
E03.setup: Corpus: all 72 answers from the original E08b runs (11,240 words). Each candidate compressed it to 600 words or fewer; gemini-3.7-flash scored facts retained out of 10, with any fabrication capping the score.

results.fabrication: YES — invented '(b) chosen by every model' contradicting the corpus

E03.finding: deepseek-v4-flash invented a claim that the corpus contradicts, which is an automatic fail. gpt-6-luna kept the most facts (9/10), glm-5.3-flash 8/10. For compression, fidelity matters more than price.

E04.question: Are any free models available as fallbacks?
E04.result: No free models were served by the router at the time of the check. stepfun/step-5-preview had moved from free to $1.00/$2.70 per million input/output tokens after its free window ended. OpenRouter listed 16 free models, but the router used here did not serve them.
E04.finding: No run needed. A free model's price can change without notice, as step-5-preview showed, so free models are a poor choice for fallback slots.

E05.question: How much of the cost difference between models comes from how much they write?
E05.setup: Derived from the effort-ladder runs (E08b: 72 kimi/deepseek runs plus 36 glm runs): mean output tokens per run, against task answers that needed roughly 150-250 words.

results.note: about 3x glm's output, a large part of why its cost per pass is higher at similar pass rates

E05.finding: Verbosity is a large cost driver. At equal unit prices, kimi's roughly 3x token volume alone would cost about 3x more; its higher unit price accounts for the rest of the gap.
E05.price_note: This entry originally quoted glm-5.3-flash output at $0.82/M; e07-prompt-cache.json records $0.6736/M and uses that figure in its cost computation. The two files record different prices.

T02-followup.result: still walled — 60 s of polling on the real browser harness, CF interstitial never resolved (0 chars throughout).
T02-followup.finding: T02 stands: neither tool gets past a real bot wall from a plain IP. Those targets need a scraping API or client-side access.

cost_note: Sum of E01 and E02 candidate costs. Grader costs, the E01 re-run and E03 were not recorded.
notes: Models were called through an OpenAI-compatible router; names and prices are as recorded at run time.
